title: Outcomes of dental implants placed in horizontally augmented or native posterior mandibular bone: a 15-year prospective cohort study
html: This study assessed and compared the 15-year clinical outcomes of dental implants placed in posterior mandibular native bone versus sites augmented solely with autologous bone. A total of 39 patients received 83 implants as part of two randomized controlled trials. Clinical and radiographic parameters, biological complications, and patient satisfaction were prospectively evaluated at baseline and after 1, 5, and 15 years after placement of the restoration. Patient satisfaction was assessed with a self-administered questionnaire using a five-point scale and a visual analogue scale (0–10).After 15 years, implant survival rates were high in both groups, reaching 94.7% in native bone and 95.3% in augmented bone.
